sections.title: How to play
sections.intro: Every arrow on the board points somewhere. Give one a tap and it slides away, as long as nothing stands in its path. Find the order that sets them all free, from a gentle first board to puzzles bigger than your screen.

items: Look where each arrow points. Its path runs straight on to the edge of the board.
Pick an arrow with nothing in front of it, and off it goes. Pick a blocked one and one of your 3 hearts is gone.
Free every arrow and the level is yours. Clearing one can only ever free others, so no level turns impossible halfway.

items.title: Stuck?
items.text: A hint points out an arrow that is free to go this moment. The first 3 are free, then they cost 30 coins.

items.title: A big board?
items.text: Drag to move around it, and pinch to see all of it.

items.title: 600 levels, 17 worlds
items.text: From Meadow to Starlight, each world with its own look, along one long map.

items.title: Every tenth level, a hard one
items.text: Bigger, always a picture, played at night, and worth 30 coins.

items.title: New obstacles as you go
items.text: Rocks, bombs, ice, mirrors, portals, shutters and colour gates, each introduced as you reach it.

items.title: A daily challenge
items.text: A fresh board each day that every player shares, with rewards across the month.

items.title: Rooms with friends
items.text: Up to 8 of you race through identical boards. Send the room's six-character code and start.

items.title: Your own maps
items.text: Build levels, share them by code, and play the ones other players made.

sections.title: On your phone too
sections.intro: Exitwise is free on Android too. Sign in with Google in the browser and on the phone, and your progress, your name and your settings come along.

items.a: Yes. Each level is built from a fixed seed, which hands every player the same board, and each one is checked to be solvable before it ships.

items.q: What counts as my best on a level?
items.a: The win with the fewest hearts lost, and between two equal wins, the faster one. Each level keeps its own best, and the panel at the end of a level shows it beside your time.

items.q: Why do the levels after a hard one feel easier?
items.a: On purpose: after each hard level come two slightly smaller boards, a breather before the climb goes on.
